text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1965432100 - Hydra (enterprise, VPC) - increased 5xxs and tail latency in eu-west-1, paging oncall:sara :rotating_light:

sara: acked. I'm oncall. grabbing context and will triage.

raj: i'm ready to pair with you. seeing spike on gateway and a big queue on dedicated-gpu-pool-hydra-eu-west. requests are queuing at the LB.

marta: Hydra PM on the line, they report customer-facing errors for some tenants. asking for ETA and mitigation plan.

sara: preliminary: warm nodes are healthy but autoscaler not kicking; something's blocking scale-up for dedicated pool. possible control-plane rate-limits.

kevin: neteng: we saw a flurry of healthcheck failures hitting the proxy sidecar, looks like 502s from model runtime replicas during rolling restart.

anika: ops: no recent deploys in eu-west, last deploy was 3h ago. CI deploy-bot shows successful.

raj: ok plan A: graceful traffic shift for Hydra tenant to eu-central warm pool (same region family) using split-horizon DNS + per-tenant routing policy. fallback B: route to hosted fallback (controlled cost).

marta: Hydra prefers private routing, they'd like to avoid hosted fallback if possible. approve plan A if we can keep session affinity.

sara: assign steps: 1) provision extra warm capacity in eu-central dedicated pool, 2) update tenant routing policy to prefer eu-central, 3) sweep short TTL DNS change (30s) for edge domain, 4) monitor client 5xx and latency, 5) revert if errors increase.

deploy-bot: provisioning request submitted: pool=dedicated-gpu-hydra-eu-central, size=6 gpus, expected ready ~8m.

incident-bot: oncall handoff triggered in 1h; current oncall=sara.

kevin: neteng: we need to change split-horizon at the edge to prioritize eu-central. I'll coordinate the DNS TTL change. Suggest setting TTL=20s and changing the CNAME at the edge.

sara: rolling canary plan: 5% of Hydra traffic -> eu-central, after 90s check metrics, then 25%, 50%, 100%. watch for regressed model outputs too (quality team).

raj: adding relevant commands:
```
# push routing override for tenant hydra
redwood routes set --tenant hydra --prefer-region eu-central --weight 5
# check current routing
redwood routes get --tenant hydra
```

kevin: DNS change ready. I'll set edge TTL to 20 and then switch split-horizon mapping at 13:18 UTC.

marta: I've told Hydra support contacts. They're ready to accept short maintenance window.

sara: canary started -> 5% to eu-central. metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 4.2% -> 0.9% for canary requests. tail latency for canary 95p = 160ms (good).

raj: memory and CPU in eu-central warm pool look healthy. no OOMs, KV cache warm.

anika: autoscaler logs show reason: `api-rate-limit` on the cluster control plane, blocked scale-up events. infra is patching control-plane token bucket now.

deploy-bot: provisioning complete: pool ready: dedicated-gpu-hydra-eu-central-01..06.

sara: increasing canary to 25%. metrics look stable after 5 minutes. moving to 50%.

marta: Hydra confirms they see fewer errors in customer dashboards. thanks team.

kevin: TTL cut and split-horizon switch executed at 13:18 UTC. note: some clients cache beyond TTL, but majority will respect.

raj: 50% -> 100% shift started. running final sweep of logs for session-affinity issues and model correctness.

sara: after 30m, all traffic now routed to eu-central for Hydra. 5xx back to baseline, latency normal.

marta: Hydra support: customers restored. requesting RCA and change to capacity-balancing to avoid future single-region pressure.

anika: control-plane fix deployed for autoscaler token bucket (bump rate limit). will monitor.

sara: follow-ups: - write postmortem with timeline and root cause (control-plane rate-limit + proxy restarts) - add automated rollback to hosted fallback if dedicated pool cannot scale in 2m - add pre-warm runbook for enterprise tenants - set up alert to warn when dedicated-pool scale events are throttled

incident-bot: incident declared resolved at 15:45 UTC. incident severity reduced to Sev3.

kevin: oncall handoff: i'll take second-watch for 2h to monitor net edge metrics.

marta: thanks everyone. sending brief to Hydra PM and scheduling 1:1 to review long-term mitigation next week. :thumbsup:

sara: closing thread, will file postmortem draft by EOD. thanks team. :pray:
